moat_against: Dermatology share loss happening now — Apoquel/Cytopoint vs Elanco Zenrelia; Key Dermatology -16% in Q2 2026
Parasiticides under price attack — lower-priced broader-label rival eroding Simparica Trio in a shrinking market
Librela safety overhang — FDA label warnings suppressed the OA growth leg; related securities litigation pending
Demand erosion — multi-year U.S. vet-visit decline and newly price-sensitive pet owners attack the pricing-power pillar
Generic erosion of legacy products (Draxxin, Rimadyl and others)
moat_for: Global scale and distribution — ~20%+ global animal-health share, roughly double the nearest rival in companion animal
Prescription brands with vet habit and switching friction (Simparica Trio, Apoquel/Cytopoint, Librela/Solensia); ~73% of the 2024 veterinary mAb market
Diversification hedge — livestock, diagnostics and international kept growing while U.S. companion fell 11% in Q2 2026
Proven economics through the cycle — OE positive 5/5 years, ~37% operating margins, pipeline guided to 12+ potential blockbusters
moat_justification: Still the scaled global leader at roughly double its nearest competitor's companion-animal share, with brands, vet-channel lock-in and a first-mover monoclonal-antibody platform — but 2026 is the first year the erosion forces are taking measurable share in two core franchises at once (dermatology to Elanco Zenrelia, parasiticides to a lower-priced broader-label rival, Librela suppressed by FDA safety warnings), which caps the score below the 8-9 this business would have earned three years ago.
name: Zoetis Inc.
one_liner: High-quality animal-health leader, moat 7/10 but eroding — does not clear 15% at $75.68 (weighted IRR 10.4%, IV@15 $46.87 vs $75.68 price); it clears 15% only at ~$46.87, so wait for that price or for proof U.S. companion share has stabilized.
